title: Floating Rates After a Promotional Period on a Home Loan: Plan Ahead
desc: Home loan with a promotional rate for the first years, then floating: how much do payments rise? How to calculate it, an example, and how to protect yourself.
summary: Explains promotional and floating rates on home loans, with an example of how monthly payments rise after the promotion and what to do to avoid defaulting.
body: p

Many home loan packages advertise a low interest rate for the first 1–3 years. After this period, the rate switches to a floating rate, usually a reference rate plus a margin. Many people only calculate payments for the promotional period and are “shocked” when they enter the third year. This article shows how to calculate in advance so you stay in control.
h2
1. What are promotional and floating rates?
ul
Promotional (fixed) rate: stays unchanged for a period stated in the contract.
Floating rate: after the promotional period, the rate is adjusted periodically (for example every 3 or 6 months) according to the formula in the contract.
p

Under Article 468 of the Civil Code, loan interest rates are agreed by the parties. Therefore, how interest is calculated after the promotion is the clause to read most carefully in the loan contract: what the reference rate is, what the margin is, and how often it is adjusted.
h2
2. Example: how much do payments rise after the promotion?
p
Assumption: a loan of VND 1 billion for 20 years, level payments; assume a rate of 7% per year for the first 2 years, then floating.
ul
First 2 years: payments of about VND 7.75 million per month. After 2 years, the remaining principal is about VND 951 million.
If the rate after the promotion is 10% per year: payments of about VND 9.51 million per month (up nearly 23%).
If 11% per year: about VND 10.13 million per month.
If 12% per year: about VND 10.76 million per month.
If 13% per year: about VND 11.41 million per month (up nearly 47% from the start).
p
The rates above are only assumptions to show sensitivity; actual rates depend on the market and each person's contract.
h2
3. A “stress test” before borrowing
ol
Calculate the monthly payment at the promotional rate.
Recalculate with an assumed rate 3–4% per year higher than the promotional rate for the remaining term.
Compare with income: if the payment in step 2 exceeds about 40% of stable income, consider reducing the loan, extending the term or choosing a cheaper home.
p
For detailed calculations, see the article “How to Calculate Monthly Home Loan Payments”.
h2
4. Terms to ask the bank about
ul
Which rate is the reference rate, where it is published, and how much margin is added.
The rate adjustment period: 1, 3 or 6 months; whether there is a cap.

Early repayment fees during and after the promotional period. Under Clause 2, Article 470 of the Civil Code, for a fixed-term loan with interest that is repaid early, all the interest for the term must still be paid, unless otherwise agreed or provided by other laws – this needs to be agreed clearly.
Consequences of late payment: penalty interest, overdue debt, and enforcement against the collateral (Article 299 of the Civil Code).
h2
5. Ways to reduce interest-rate risk
ul
Use the promotional period to pay down principal (if the early repayment fee is reasonable) – with a lower balance, a rate increase has less impact.
Keep a reserve fund of at least 6 months of payments calculated at the post-promotion rate.

If you qualify for social housing, consider a preferential loan through the Vietnam Bank for Social Policies – the interest rate is set by the State (Decree 261/2025/ND-CP amended Clause 4, Article 48 of Decree 100/2024/ND-CP to set it at 5.4% per year).
Monitor interest rates periodically; when the gap is large, ask the bank about adjusting or refinancing the loan, and calculate the incidental fees carefully.
note

This article is for reference only and is not financial advice. The interest rates in the example are assumptions, not the rates of any specific bank. Consider your ability to repay and ask the bank carefully about the floating-rate formula before signing. Social housing interest rates may be adjusted by decision of the Prime Minister.
